judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definitions identify the parties by name and by capitalized label with no vague term; "the person that is identified under the heading 'Customer' above" is definite even though the form field is blank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the arbitration section, which separately expands "we" and "us" to include officers and affiliates, and with the Lender's naming elsewhere; the only slight friction is that Lender is defined but not made a party signatory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The services list is enumerated but hedged with soft terms — "attempt to," "where available," "certain CAB services," "estimated period ... one day" — so the actual scope of what is promised for the fee is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits reasonably with the COST AND PAYMENT TERMS clause (fee earned in advance) though the statement that no fee is owed if the loan is denied must be harmonised with that; nothing squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence with a single clear proposition — the fee is not interest but is included in the TILA finance charge; no term invites two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the COST AND PAYMENT TERMS clause's breakdown of the Finance Charge into lender interest plus CAB fee, so it is consistent with the whole.
judgments.clause_name: Disclosure of Fee as Finance Charge

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is riddled with blanks and mechanical corruption ("based upon °% annualized rate," "Joan payments," "CAB fee for this transaction ofS"), and the fee is said to be "earned in advance" yet subject to a prorated "partial rebate" for the "final period," a phrase whose measure is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "earned in advance" characterisation and the payment-application order sit in some tension with the cancellation notices promising return of payments "without any penalty or obligation," and with the acknowledgment that all necessary spaces are completed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Amounts and triggers are largely specific, but "the State Allowed Returned Item Fee, whichever is greater" is an undefined referent and the closing "attorneys' fees, and costs of collection" is an open-ended catch-all attached to a specific list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the LOC reimbursement clause and the Collection Expenses clause (which adds a reasonableness limit on attorneys' fees), creating a modest question which controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause ends in plainly corrupted and truncated text ("unlgyuful excess," "maximug peepee law," "we may calculate charges by amortiz"), a mechanical defect that leaves the final sentence without a completed meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its usury-savings tail duplicates the separate COMPLIANCE clause, and its automatic revocation on cancellation must be read with the three-day Notice of Cancellation; that is harmonisable but not seamless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "If you fail to perform your other promises to us" is an open-ended catch-all beside the specific payment default, and "any other right or remedy allowed by law" widens it further; the acceleration of "your obligations, less any unearned charges" also leaves the fee treatment uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The right to "seek collection of any check or similar security" sits against the Collection Expenses clause's statement that criminal charges may not be threatened or pursued over a check given as security, a live tension in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver list is enumerated and conventional, but "others responsible" is undefined and each item is qualified by "to the extent permitted by law," leaving the operative reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The statement that "we are not required to file suit or arbitrate" brushes against the mandatory-on-election arbitration provision and the pre-suit notice requirement, though the two can be harmonised as a no-diligence clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver itself is explicit, but it speaks of not "reject[ing]" the arbitration agreement whereas the arbitration section provides an "opt out," a small vocabulary mismatch.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the No Jury Trial paragraph and the Opting Out paragraph; if the customer opts out the jury waiver still purportedly applies, which is coherent but is the kind of interaction parties argue over.
judgments.clause_name: Waiver of Right to Trial by Jury

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard usury-savings language with definite mechanics (credit or refund, automatic reduction to the maximum lawful rate); nothing in it carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the savings language in the LOC clause, and duplication here is harmless rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any claim that this agreement or related matter, or any action or inaction by us or Lender, or by any other person, is legally non-compliant" is a sweeping catch-all, and "a reasonable opportunity of not less than 60 days" plus "any corrective action shall relieve us ... of any liability" are both open at the edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As a condition precedent to "initiating any claim" it sits awkwardly with the arbitration provision permitting either side to elect arbitration "at any time" and with the small-claims carve-out in the Claim definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause mixes a fee obligation with a statutory-style prohibition whose subject is the indefinite "a person," and closes on "or other criminal conduct" after forgery, fraud and theft — a classic catch-all after specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stands against the Default clause's right to "seek collection of any check or similar security you have provided us," and this criminal-complaint issue is precisely where the parties' positions in this instrument diverge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single stipulation with no operative variable; "for all purposes" is broad but the proposition is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the FAA governing-law choice in the arbitration provision and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short definite sentences; "at our discretion" is one-sided but its meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the arbitration provision's extension of "we" to affiliates and with the Entire Agreement clause; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely informational addresses and phone number; no operative term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Chicago address matches the notice addresses in the pre-suit notice and cancellation forms, save that the opt-out notice is addressed to "PLS Financial Services" — a naming variance in that other clause, not this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The blunt statement that Claims will be arbitrated "instead of having them decided in court" is stated absolutely, without the qualifications (election, opt-out, small claims) that follow, so read alone it overstates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the Opting Out paragraph, the small-claims carve-out, the pre-suit notice clause and the jury waiver; whether the obligation is mandatory or elective is exactly the kind of question this instrument invites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition enumerates categories then adds "(d) the actions of you, us, Lender, or third parties," an almost boundless catch-all, and the exclusions turn on "properly exercised an opt-out right," a phrase whose content lies elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the Opting Out paragraph (which limits exclusion to claims "arising under this Agreement") and with the pre-suit notice clause, leaving the treatment of prior-transaction and third-party claims contestable.
judgments.clause_name: Definition of Claim — Arbitration Agreement and Limitation on Class Participation

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Either you, we, or Lender may give written notice ... at any time, even if the other party has begun a lawsuit" is definite in wording, but "reasonably satisfactory to us" and the seller's fallback right to select the arbitrator are one-sidedly drafted openings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The right to demand arbitration "at any time" despite an existing lawsuit runs against the pre-suit notice clause and the Notices and Waivers statement that "we are not required to ... arbitrate," and raises the waiver question this contract's structure leaves open.
judgments.clause_name: Starting an Arbitration/Costs — election to arbitrate any Claim

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly definite, but the venue list ends with "or such other location as we or Lender may agree" — agreement with whom is unstated — and there is a stray comma splice before "Unless the arbitrator determines."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the FAA choice in the Governing Law clause and the cost-advance provisions; no contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, mechanically clear provision about entering judgment and the deemed situs of the award.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the FAA governing-law clause and the arbitration procedure paragraph; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics (30 days, writing, stated address) are definite, though the address names "PLS Financial Services" rather than the contracting entity and "arising under this Agreement" is narrower than the Claim definition's reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the Definition of Claim, which sweeps in prior agreements and third-party actions, the effect of an opt-out on those claims is not fully resolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain, explanatory language tied to the election of arbitration; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the separate WAIVER OF RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY clause, which purports to waive jury trial in litigation regardless; the overlap is harmonisable but not identical in effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver is repeated emphatically and covers representative, private-attorney-general and joinder capacities, so its own terms are clear; the conditional opening "if either you, we, or Lender ... choose arbitration" leaves its operation before any election slightly open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with the arbitration-organization selection rule barring class-permitting organizations and with severability; the residual question is its effect if the customer opts out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability and a conflict rule favouring the agreement over the organization's code; both sentences are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the Entire Agreement clause's reformation provision without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence choice of law with a clearly carved-out exception; the only softness is that the FAA does not supply a full body of substantive law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the arbitration provision's own FAA clause and the Interstate Commerce stipulation; consistent, with only a minor question about which law fills gaps in arbitrability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cautionary disclosure in the form of advice; it creates no obligation and no term needs construing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a notice rather than an operative promise, so it does not collide with the fee or default terms; at most it colours the product's short-term character.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely a contact notice with definite details.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the pre-suit notice and arbitration provisions as an administrative avenue; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Relating to the subject matter of this Agreement" is a familiar but elastic boundary, and the reformation sentence uses "if practicable," which is a judgment call; still the clause's core is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The integration language must accommodate the separate Credit Services Disclosure Statement and the two Notices of Cancellation acknowledged in the signature block, plus the loan documents with the Lender, so its exclusivity is not airtight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is specific, but sub-item (2) certifies receipt of "THIS CREDIT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ALL NECESSARY SPACES COMPLETED" and the warranty of no "intention to file a petition" is an inherently subjective term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The completed-spaces certification is contradicted on the face of this form, whose COST AND PAYMENT TERMS figures are blank, and the integration clause sits against the acknowledged separate disclosure statement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Before midnight of the third day after the date of the transaction" is a definite deadline, but it measures from the transaction date whereas the attached form measures from signing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That mismatch with the Notice of Cancellation forms ("within three days after the date the contract is signed") is a specific internal inconsistency in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and clear on its face; "without any penalty or obligation" is broad but its meaning in a cancellation notice is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs against the front-page NOTICE measuring from "the date of the transaction" and against the CAB fee being "earned in advance at the inception of the loan."
judgments.clause_name: Notice of Cancellation — Right to Cancel

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite refund obligation with a stated 10-day period keyed to receipt of the notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the LOC clause's automatic revocation on timely cancellation, though it does not address amounts already advanced by the Lender.
judgments.clause_name: Notice of Cancellation — Return of Payments

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence ends "not later than midnight on" with the date left blank, so the operative deadline in the very form that fixes it is missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That blank must be filled from the front-page three-day notice, whose measuring date differs from this form's "date the contract is signed," leaving the cancellation deadline unsettled across the instrument.
judgments.clause_name: Notice of Cancellation — How to Cancel
